test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2024: Official Paper (Held On: 01 Jul, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Dhruv’s __anger blazed of__ uncontrollably.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. 'anger blazed up'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"blazed"** means to burn fiercely or brightly; it can also refer to something that is displayed intensely. (जल उठना)

 
 
• **Example:** The campfire blazed brightly in the night, providing warmth to the campers.
 
 
 
• **"Blazed up"** refers to the sudden or intense outburst of something, usually fire or emotion. (भड़क उठना)
 
 
• **Example:** His anger blazed up when he heard the unfair decision.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct phrase is **'anger blazed up'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. 'anger blazed up'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **anger blazed after** (क्रोध बाद में भड़क उठा): This phrase is incorrect as it suggests a sequence of events rather than an immediate reaction.

 
 
• **Example:** His anger blazed after he learned the truth, but this is not the same context as the sentence given.
 
 
 
• **anger blazed into** (क्रोध में बदल गया): This phrase is incorrect as it implies transformation rather than an outburst.
 
 
• **Example:** His frustration blazed into anger, but it changes the meaning of the original sentence.
 
 
 
• **anger blazed onwards** (क्रोध आगे बढ़ गया): This phrase is incorrect as it suggests continuation rather than an outburst.
 
 
• **Example:** His anger blazed onwards, but it does not fit the context of the original sentence.
 
 

45:Tcff,

The correct answer is: **Option 3**.
